purpose: Test query adaptation, evidence classification, provenance independence, causal-link reasoning, and uncertainty handling. No values describe real tutoring programs or students.
task: Explain whether after-school mathematics tutoring improves outcomes, how it might work, and for whom.

sources.title: Synthetic Trial A: Randomized Tutoring Offer in Two Districts
sources.design: Individual randomized offer; volunteer schools; 420 lower-secondary pupils
sources.population_scope: Two districts; pupils whose families opted into the study
sources.comparison: Offer of weekly tutoring versus usual school support
sources.outcome: Standardized mathematics test at six months
sources.mechanism_evidence: Attendance was measured during the program and was higher in the offer group; the study did not identify the causal effect of attendance or feedback on test outcomes.
limitations: Volunteer schools and families limit generalization.
The randomized offer estimates the offer effect, not the causal effect of each mediator.

sources.title: Synthetic Trial B: Cluster-Randomized Tutoring Across Twelve Schools
sources.population_scope: One region; all enrolled pupils in participating schools
sources.outcome: Standardized mathematics test at one academic year
sources.finding: Average intention-to-treat difference +0.01 SD (95% CI -0.08 to +0.10), compatible with little or no average effect.
sources.mechanism_evidence: A positive estimate among high-attendance pupils was exploratory and post hoc; attendance was not randomized, so it does not establish a dose effect.
limitations: The subgroup analysis was not prespecified and is not confirmatory.

sources.title: Synthetic Cohort C: Tutoring Participation and Later Mathematics Scores
sources.finding: Adjusted association +0.17 SD after matching on recorded prior achievement and demographics.
limitations: Unmeasured motivation, family support, and selection may remain.
The adjusted association alone does not identify a causal effect.

sources.title: Synthetic Review D: Summary of Tutoring Evidence
sources.design: Narrative summary; no new participants or analysis
sources.population_scope: Inherits the scope of cited sources
sources.finding: Repeats the positive estimates reported by SYN-RCT-A and SYN-COHORT-C.
limitations: Not independent replication; it reuses existing source families.

expected_observations: Recognize that the two synthetic randomized estimates differ and retain both rather than selecting only the favorable one.
Distinguish the randomized offer effect from observational participation association and from attendance/feedback mediation.
Do not count SYN-REVIEW-D as an independent data source or replication of SYN-RCT-A.
Use terms such as intention-to-treat, cluster trial, attendance dose, and post-hoc subgroup to make a justified next retrieval move.
Keep effect size, population limits, and uncertainty separate; do not infer universal benefit or no benefit from this small packet.
